## Pedagogical Vision

Classical machine learning curricula operate entirely **behind glass**: a misplaced class label or high prediction error results in a software retry or log entry. **Physical AI begins when software commands physical actuators**—mass moves, friction generates heat, kinetic energy is spent, and the physical world permanently transitions ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, u_t)$). You cannot `ctrl+z` kinetic energy.

This course teaches the systems engineering disciplines required for that transition:
$$\text{Observe} \longrightarrow \text{Estimate} \longrightarrow \text{Intend} \longrightarrow \text{Plan} \longrightarrow \text{Enforce}$$

The central invariant governing the course is the **Proposal–Permission Boundary**:

1. **The Cognitive Cortex (Linux MPU):** Runs deep multimodal foundation models (VLMs), spatial tokenizers (DINOv2), and generative action chunking decoders (Diffusion Policy / ACT). It generates timestamped, expiring intent proposals.
2. **The Safety Enforcer (Real-Time MCU):** Runs a bare-metal, zero-allocation $1000\text{ Hz}$ control loop. It verifies Control Barrier Functions ($h(x) \ge 0$), monitors dynamic stopping distances ($d_{\text{stop}}$), and commands motor gate inverters.

Because students enter this curriculum from diverse engineering backgrounds, the course provides three tailored conceptual pathways:

* **Pathway A · The Machine Learning Practitioner:** Emphasizes the thermodynamic and kinematic consequences of model decisions. Focuses on why open-loop statistical accuracy fails in dynamic environments, how memory bandwidth bounds inference frequency ($t_{\text{stream}} = M_{\text{weights}} / B_{\text{mem}}$), why compounding covariate drift requires closed-loop exposure bounds, and how to interface unprivileged neural models with deterministic real-time supervisors (Key Chapters: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation, @sec-intent, @sec-enforcement, @sec-release).
* **Pathway B · The Robotics & Control Engineer:** Emphasizes augmenting classical analytical dynamics with high-capacity learned foundation models. Focuses on open-vocabulary 3D semantic grounding, learning multimodal action distributions via trajectory diffusion without mode collapse, and enforcing Control Barrier Function (CBF-QP) safety shields over learned trajectory proposals (Key Chapters: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous, @sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-verification).
* **Pathway C · The Embedded & Silicon Architect:** Emphasizes heterogeneous system partitioning, hardware arbitration, and deterministic safety enforcement. Focuses on multi-rate clock cadences, lock-free seqlocks with memory barriers, AXI QoS bus arbitration under neural DMA bursts, inductive voltage droop ($L \, dI/dt$), and hardware fault injection (Key Chapters: @sec-boundary, @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-memory, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement, @sec-intervention, @sec-verification).

## The 14-Week Curriculum & Laboratory Spine

The course is structured across 17 textbook chapters and 14 laboratory studio sessions:

### Part I: The machine anatomy (weeks 1–3)

* **Week 1 · Kit Bring-Up & The Closed Loop (@sec-boundary):**
  * *Lecture:* The causal loop ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, u_t)$), state mutation, idempotency loss, and the first-exhausted physical budget.
  * *Studio Lab (`00-kit-bringup`, `01-close-the-loop`):* Dual-brain IPC setup, safe idle transitions, open-loop vs closed-loop telemetry.
  * *Deliverable:* **Loop Charter**.
* **Week 2 · Reflected Inertia & Actuator Dynamics (@sec-body):**
  * *Lecture:* Reflected rotor inertia ($N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$), QDD vs. Harmonic drives, and thermal impedance networks ($\Delta T = P \cdot \theta_{\text{JA}}$).
  * *Studio Lab (`02-freshness-wall`):* Inverter current shunt measurement, thermal step response, stopping distance bounds.
* **Week 3 · The Two-Speed Brain & Multi-Rate Pipelines (@sec-brain, @sec-nervous):**
  * *Lecture:* Slow deliberative foundation models ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$) vs. fast reflex enforcers ($1000\text{ Hz}$); lock-free seqlocks, deterministic fieldbuses (EtherCAT DC), and the Master 5x5 Synthesis Grid.
  * *Studio Lab (`03-measure-both-brains`, `04-runtime-fault-containment`):* $P_{99}$ latency profiling, inter-processor seqlock buffers, MPU crash survival.
  * *Deliverable:* **Requirements Ledger**.

### Part II: Teaching the machine (weeks 4–5)

* **Week 4 · Data Foundations & Teleoperation (@sec-data):**
  * *Lecture:* Compounding covariate shift, distribution drift, bilateral teleoperation latency, multi-stream synchronous logging, and Open X-Embodiment datasets.
  * *Studio Lab (`04-dma-tokens`):* Human demonstration capture, teleoperation jitter compensation, action space normalization.
  * *Deliverable:* **Observation Contract**.
* **Week 5 · Policy Synthesis Regimes & Closed-Loop Survival Testing (@sec-training, @sec-evaluation):**
  * *Lecture:* Imitation learning (ACT, Diffusion Policy) vs. reinforcement learning, sim-to-real domain randomization, compounding drift ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$), and the Butler & Finelli exposure wall ($N \ge 3/p_{\max}$) with exact Clopper-Pearson confidence bounds.
  * *Studio Lab (`05-policy-synthesis`, `06-survival-bench`):* Continuous diffusion action chunking, closed-loop rollout testing, non-asymptotic hardware bench failure rate estimation.
  * *Deliverable:* **Policy Evaluation Report**.

### Part III: Running the machine (weeks 6–9)

* **Week 6 · Perception & 3D Spatial Encoders (@sec-perception):**
  * *Lecture:* Sensor latency waterfalls, rolling shutter distortion, on-manifold IMU preintegration, and open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs.
  * *Studio Lab (`07-perception-frontier`):* MIPI CSI-2 direct memory access (DMA) ring buffers, camera-to-IMU temporal calibration, spatial feature tokenization.
  * *Deliverable:* **Perception Model**.
* **Week 7 · Spatial Memory & Intent Grounding (@sec-memory, @sec-intent):**
  * *Lecture:* $SE(3)$ coordinate frame trees, volumetric raycasting (3D-DDA), TSDFs, covariance expansion, Vision-Language Models (VLMs) as unprivileged proposal engines, spatial affordances, and expiring intent leases.
  * *Studio Lab (`08-belief-drift`, `09-two-speed-intent`):* Timestamp skew mitigation, occupancy voxel updates, belief lease expiration, edge VLM prompt parsing, 3D target bounding, intent lease TTL enforcement.
  * *Deliverable:* **State & Intent Schema**.
* **Week 8 · Trajectory Planning & Seam Continuity (@sec-planning):**
  * *Lecture:* Receding-horizon planning, $\mathcal{C}^2$ cubic/quintic jerk-bounded splines, trajectory chunk seam blending, stopping distance contingency maneuvers, and stopping suffixes.
  * *Studio Lab (`10-trajectory-seams`):* Real-time spline generation, chunk boundary smoothing, trajectory seam torque limit enforcement.
  * *Deliverable:* **Trajectory Design**.
* **Week 9 · The Signature Enforcer & Heterogeneous Placement (@sec-enforcement, @sec-placement):**
  * *Lecture:* Control Barrier Functions (CBFs), active-set barrier quadratic programming (QP), minimal intervention safety shields, AXI crossbar contention, memory bandwidth walls (MemGuard), and PDN inductive voltage droop ($\Delta V = L \cdot dI/dt$).
  * *Studio Lab (`11-mcu-enforcer`, `12-placement-ripple`):* **Signature Lab & Midterm Milestone:** Bare-metal $1000\text{ Hz}$ MCU CBF veto filter overriding invalid MPU trajectory proposals under bus contention and memory stress.
  * *Deliverable:* **Enforcement & Placement Design**.

### Part IV: Governing the machine (weeks 10–12)

* **Week 10 · Human Intervention & Shared Autonomy (@sec-intervention):**
  * *Lecture:* Shared control policy blending, bumpless control transfer, and human takeover reaction times.
  * *Studio Lab (`13-shadow-and-faults`, `14-authority-paths`):* Bumpless joystick override, state-conditioned authority arbitration.
  * *Deliverable:* **Authority Design**.
* **Week 11 · Verification & Synthetic Falsification (@sec-verification):**
  * *Lecture:* The 4-stage qualification ladder (Sim $\to$ PIL $\to$ HIL $\to$ In-Situ), temporal logic falsification, and hardware-in-the-loop stress testing.
  * *Studio Lab (`15-fault-injection`):* Cross-layer fault injection (dropped packets, voltage sags, optical occlusion).
* **Week 12 · Release Assurance & Safety Cases (@sec-release):**
  * *Lecture:* Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) safety cases, Goal Structuring Notation (GSN), and UL 4600 / ISO standard alignment.
  * *Studio Lab (`99-design-review` prep):* Cryptographic artifact signing, safety case construction, release gate audit.
  * *Deliverable:* **Release Case**.

### Capstone: The physical intelligence frontier (weeks 13–14)

* **Weeks 13–14 · Capstone Jury & Unannounced Fault Defense (@sec-frontier):**
  * *Lecture:* Unsolved frontiers of physical AI, epistemic limits, and long-tail generalization across physical embodiments.
  * *Studio Defense:* Live capstone demonstration. The teaching team injects unannounced real-time hardware/sensor faults. Teams must prove that their physical agent either safely achieves the task or transitions into a certified safe holding state without mechanical impact.
  * *Deliverable:* **Final Signed Release Verdict**.

## Grading & Assessment Policy

This course employs a **Project-First, Continuous-Evidence Evaluation** model without classical written exams:

| Component                     | Weight | Assessment Criteria                                                                                                                                      |
|:------------------------------|:------:|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Studio Labs & Checkpoints** |  25%   | Timely execution of weekly bench milestones, hardware wiring integrity, and working firmware builds.                                                     |
| **Engineering Notebook**      |  35%   | Rigorous, version-controlled records of latency distributions ($P_{50}, P_{90}, P_{99}$), energy budgets, and system logs across all chapter milestones. |
| **Midterm Enforcement Gate**  |  15%   | Formal verification and live bench demonstration of the signature 1 kHz MCU Control Barrier Function enforcer.                                           |
| **Capstone System Defense**   |  25%   | Live final demonstration defending the Physical Agent against unannounced seeded faults before the faculty jury.                                         |
